decisions.reason: As a prominently presented core office-furniture innovation, it is likely still near aspiration levels and an established firm would give it more time before reallocating resources.
A chair family fits the firm’s mainstream furniture business, and its stand-alone presentation suggests sufficient early commitment to retain it while results remain uncertain.
This is a more experimental adjacent product, but because it had its own page and the firm likely has some slack, management would more likely continue monitoring than drop it immediately.
Being only mentioned rather than fully presented signals weaker internal support and likely performance below aspiration, making it the strongest candidate for resource reallocation.
A high standing table is close to established office-furniture capabilities, so a mature German manufacturer would usually keep it on the market unless there were clearer signs of underperformance.

The rug collection is somewhat peripheral to core furniture, but dedicated website treatment indicates enough commitment that management would likely keep it for another year while learning from the market.
